title: Incident playbook dispatcher that selects runbooks and orchestrates PagerDuty/Slack notifications
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: Our current incident notifications send generic PagerDuty and Slack alerts with static runbook links. On-call engineers still spend too much time triaging noise, reconstructing trace slices, and deciding which runbook steps are relevant. Goal: Build an automated 'playbook dispatcher' that consumes an incoming alert (metrics/trace/log signal), scores probable root-cause categories, composes a focused runbook fragment, and orchestrates targeted PagerDuty/Slack actions with contextual attachments and interactive choices for the responder. This should reduce time-to-action for high-severity incidents, reduce noisy wakeups for low-confidence signals, and produce structured post-incident artifacts for automatic postmortem seeding.
design_notes: High-level design and mockups: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Playbook+Dispatcher+Design. Prototype sketches live in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PlaybookDispatcher. Key decisions: use trace-span sampling heuristics + metric anomaly classifiers for pre-scoring; expose a configurable confidence threshold per service; include a short-circuit path that suppresses PD for low-confidence-but-not-critical signals; provide Slack interactive buttons (Acknowledge / Run fragments / Escalate) that call internal orchestration API; persist chosen fragment and responder choices to audit log. UX mockups reviewed by Design (Sofia Ramirez) on 2026-03-09.
implementation_plan:
1) Ingest alerts: extend observability webhook adapter to emit normalized AlertContext (trace ids, metric slices, top-k spans).
2) Scoring: implement a microservice `playbook-scoring` that applies rule-based and ML-style heuristics to produce category+confidence.
3) Fragment assembler: map category -> runbook fragments, merge with service-specific instructions and prefilled remediation commands.
4) Notification orchestrator: extend PD connector to optionally create PD incident with `auto_preferred_response` based on confidence; extend Slack notifier to post thread starter with attachments and interactive buttons.
5) Audit + postmortem seeding: write chosen fragment, trace excerpt, responder actions to PostmortemSeed store and emit event to postmortem generator.
6) Observability + metrics: add dashboards to monitor dispatcher impact (time-to-ack, suppressed PD rate, false-suppression incidents).
7) Rollout: pilot for three internal services behind feature flag; collect metrics for 2 weeks; iterate.
acceptance_criteria: Dispatcher receives synthetic alerts and returns category+confidence within 200ms median latency.
Slack thread posts include trace snippet, top-3 suspect spans, and 3 actionable runbook steps with prefilled commands.
PagerDuty incidents are created only for alerts above configurable confidence threshold; suppressions produce audit entries and a Slack summary channel message.
PostmortemSeed entries are created for every PagerDuty-triggered incident with linked trace and the selected runbook fragment.
Dashboards show a measurable reduction (>15%) in median time-to-first-action for pilot services after 2 weeks.
risks: False suppressions for novel failure modes could delay critical response; mitigation: conservative default thresholds and PD override button.
Data privacy: trace excerpts may contain PII; mitigation: runbook assembler must apply redaction policies and KMS-backed audit logs.
Operational complexity: additional microservice increases surface area; mitigation: include health-checks, circuit-breakers, and fallback to existing notification path.
ML heuristics may bias toward past outage patterns; mitigation: include human-in-the-loop feedback and decay windows for training signals.
